superradiance_condition.fidelity: exact - uses standard Kerr metric formula

hydrogenic_approximation.fidelity: standard approximation, valid for alpha < 0.5; extended to alpha < 1.0 with caveats
hydrogenic_approximation.deviation: For alpha > 0.5, the hydrogenic approximation becomes less accurate. We cap alpha at sqrt(2*n^2)*0.99 to prevent unphysical results. Full numerical calculation would require solving the Teukolsky equation.

regge_trajectory.fidelity: analytic result from superradiance boundary condition

instability_timescale.fidelity: leading-order approximation from Detweiler (1980) and Arvanitaki et al. (2010)
instability_timescale.deviation: Higher-order corrections and exact numerical factors are omitted. The timescale is approximate but sufficient for order-of-magnitude comparison with astrophysical timescales.

bayesian_posterior_propagation.definition: P(excl|data,mu) = integral of indicator function over posterior p(M,a*|data)
bayesian_posterior_propagation.fidelity: exact Monte Carlo estimate using posterior samples
bayesian_posterior_propagation.notes: This is the key innovation: using full posterior distributions rather than point estimates

self_interaction_bosenova.definition: Superradiance shuts down when N_max > N_crit ~ (f_a/mu)^2
self_interaction_bosenova.deviation: The actual bosenova dynamics are more complex, involving periodic collapses and regrowth. Our treatment assumes complete shutdown, which is conservative.

joint_constraints.fidelity: assumes independence of the two BH measurements
